newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Prices still seen vulnerable on downside.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Prices still seen vulnerable on downside.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures are likely to remain vulnerable on the downside, although the yen's weakening against the dollar may provide support, traders said on Monday.

"Backed by the yen's slip, a moderate rebound in rubber futures is likely after the selloff last week. But private investors may be quick to take advantage of any price rebound to sell," an analyst at a commodity brokerage said.

The analyst said fragile physical demand in rubber producing countries and mounting pressure from rising Japanese rubber stocks in the near term are likely to prevent the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM)'s benchmark September futures from breaking above 150 yen per kg this week.
TOCOM September rubber ended the morning session at 146.1 yen per kg, against 145.0 yen at Friday's close.
Similarly, the benchmark September contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 146.8 yen per kg, compared with 146.00 yen on Friday.
The market is focusing largely on the currency market, watching to see how much further the yen will slip against the dollar.
The dollar rose to 124.83 yen, its highest level since February 1993, in early Tokyo trade on Monday.
Traders said activity in the rubber markets would continue to be sluggish, as static prices in recent months have dampened investor interest.

In addition, commodity brokers are recommending that private investors put money into the newly launched yen-based aluminium futures contract and this could lessen activity in the rubber futures market even further, traders said.

Talk that the Thai government may buy more Thai benchmark Ribbed Smoked Sheet (RSS) 3 rubber, in an effort to prop up the sagging markets, were though unlikely to give much support to Japanese prices.

"The effect of any intervention by the Thai government is in doubt. Market players believe the government may find it difficult to sell rubber, as rubber-consuming countries may be more interested in purchasing cheaper Indonesian Technically Specified Rubber (TSR)," a trading house trader said.
The offer price for Thai rubber to Japan was quoted at 120 cents per kg on Monday, against 122 cents as of March 31.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 159 yen per kg on Monday, compared with 164 yen as of March 31.
